predictions.reasoning: OpenAI is private, so the most liquid public proxy for an AGI-related surprise is the AI hardware/megacap complex. A sharp jump in the implied probability of OpenAI declaring AGI would signal accelerating capability/compute demand, which markets historically translate into upside for the dominant AI accelerator supplier. However, absent an actual public announcement, an AGI declaration is an extremely low-base-rate, hard-to-verify event; a probability move on a thin Polymarket contract is a very noisy sensor and unlikely to move NVDA the full 700bps threshold in 12h.

predictions.reasoning: Microsoft has the deepest public financial linkage to OpenAI, so an OpenAI AGI milestone is the cleanest single-name transmission channel. But the direction is genuinely ambiguous: an AGI declaration could be read bullishly (commercial dominance) or introduce regulatory, governance, and even IP-ownership uncertainty (Microsoft's OpenAI agreement contains AGI-related clauses that could limit access). Because the market event lacks confirmation and the sign is uncertain, this is a weak, low-confidence mapping.

llm_justification.summary: This market maps to public assets only indirectly, since OpenAI is private. The cleanest liquid proxies are NVIDIA (AI-hardware sentiment) and Microsoft (largest public OpenAI stakeholder). A sharp rise in the implied probability of an OpenAI AGI declaration would nominally be bullish for AI capability plays, but the event is extremely low base-rate, hard to verify, and the sign for Microsoft is ambiguous due to AGI-related contract clauses. Both mappings are weak and low-confidence; a Polymarket probability move without an actual public announcement is most likely noise rather than leaked information.
key_assumptions: A meaningful move in the market's implied probability occurred
No official public AGI announcement has yet been made (otherwise it is already priced)
NVDA/MSFT remain the most exposed liquid proxies for OpenAI-related news
Market participants would interpret an AGI signal as broadly AI-bullish
failure_modes: The Polymarket move is speculative noise on a thin contract with no real information content
Any actual AGI news would be public instantly and already reflected in prices, leaving no edge
Microsoft could fall rather than rise if AGI declaration triggers governance/IP-access concerns
Proxies (NVDA/MSFT) are only weakly exposed to a private-company milestone and may not move at all
The 700bps tradability threshold is very unlikely to be met absent a genuine confirmed announcement
